name: Copernicus Wrocław Airport
before:
Poland's fifth busiest airport, ten kilometres west of Wroclaw, handling more than 3.8 million passengers in 2023.

Everything works from one runway and one passenger terminal, with separate cargo and general aviation terminals alongside. The international departures hall has a duty free area. The cargo terminal is better equipped than the size suggests, with 3,300 square metres of storage, a bonded warehouse, a freezer and a store for radioactive materials.

Buses do the work of getting into the city. MPK Wroclaw lines 106 by day and 206 at night both run to the main railway station and the main bus station, with plenty of stops along the way.

This is a joint civil and military field, used by the Polish Air Force, the United States Air Force, NATO and the Heavy Airlift Wing, so military movements are routine. The airport is named after Nicolaus Copernicus.
after:
Poland's fifth busiest airport, ten kilometres west of Wrocław, with a single runway. It handled about 4.9 million passengers in 2025, on Eurostat's figures.

City buses do the work of getting into town. Line 106 runs by day to the main railway station and night bus 206 to the main bus station, both with plenty of stops along the way.

The airport is named after Nicolaus Copernicus.

claims.note: Eurostat's 2025 table of every Polish airport it reports: Warsaw Chopin, Krakow, Gdansk and Katowice, then Wroclaw with 4,900,785, ahead of Poznan.

claims.note: Was 'more than 3.8 million passengers in 2023' (Eurostat 3,880,957). A passenger total replaces a passenger total: Eurostat has 4,900,785 for 2025. The operator's site refused a plain request and the browser (403) and the civil aviation office's statistics could not be reached, so the figure is attributed to Eurostat.

claims.claim: city buses: 106 by day to the main railway station, night bus 206 to the main bus station, many stops
claims.inAfter: Line 106 runs by day to the main railway station and night bus 206 to the main bus station, both with plenty of stops along the way.
claims.note: Was 'MPK Wroclaw lines 106 by day and 206 at night both run to the main railway station and the main bus station'. The city's own timetables run 106 from PORT LOTNICZY to DWORZEC GLOWNY (the main railway station) and list 206 among the night buses, from PORT LOTNICZY to DWORZEC AUTOBUSOWY (the bus station); each route passes several streets. The MPK name rests on Wikipedia alone, so the text says city buses.

claims.wasBefore: handling more than 3.8 million passengers in 2023.
claims.why: Superseded by the 2025 total. Corrected (see above).

claims.claim: one passenger terminal, with separate cargo and general aviation terminals
claims.wasBefore: Everything works from one runway and one passenger terminal, with separate cargo and general aviation terminals alongside.
claims.why: The terminals rest on Wikipedia alone, which contradicts itself (its lead says one passenger terminal, its facilities section 'domestic, international and cargo terminals'), and the operator's site refused a plain request and the browser (403). The single runway is kept (see above).

claims.claim: a duty free area in the international departures hall
claims.wasBefore: The international departures hall has a duty free area.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the operator's site could not be read.

claims.claim: the cargo terminal: 3,300 m2, a bonded warehouse, a freezer, a radioactive materials store
claims.wasBefore: The cargo terminal is better equipped than the size suggests, with 3,300 square metres of storage, a bonded warehouse, a freezer and a store for radioactive materials.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the operator's site could not be read, and a count or specification could only come back as the airport's own, attributed.

claims.claim: MPK Wroclaw runs the lines; both lines to both stations
claims.wasBefore: MPK Wroclaw lines 106 by day and 206 at night both run to the main railway station and the main bus station
claims.why: The city's timetables give each line one end: 106 at the main railway station, 206 at the bus station. The MPK name rests on Wikipedia alone. Corrected (see above).

claims.claim: a joint civil and military field used by the Polish Air Force, the USAF, NATO and the Heavy Airlift Wing
claims.wasBefore: This is a joint civil and military field, used by the Polish Air Force, the United States Air Force, NATO and the Heavy Airlift Wing, so military movements are routine.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and partly out of date on its own account (the 3rd Air Base that shared the runway was reformed in 2010). The 2019 US and Polish defence declaration that Wikipedia cites sets up an aerial port of debarkation without naming Wroclaw on the page read (the White House archive), so it cannot be the second source.
